cases.why: verify-identity CREATED. The opaque applicantId is the WHOLE payload.
Idempotent replay, same applicantId as the original 201.
INVARIANT 2, THE LOAD-BEARING FIXTURE. nationalIdHash is an internal cross-service join key and must never reach a browser. The deprecated useWalkIn hook asked the browser to COMPUTE one.
INVARIANT 2. The raw NID is request-only. It never appears in a response, a log line, or an event.
The NIDA record's name, DOB and gender are encrypted at rest and never returned by this edge.
channel is REQUIRED. The deprecated NIDA hook omitted it, so every call would have been a 400.
400 INVALID_CHANNEL. This exact omission was the deprecated frontend's bug.
Four channels only: WEB, USSD, IREMBO_KIOSK, WALK_IN.
ONE uniform 202 across at least four input classes: known applicant, unknown id, no phone on record, rate-limited repeat.
A masked-phone hint is a designed leak: it confirms the national id exists AND that a number is on file. The API refused to leak it; the UI must not reintroduce it.
The ONLY place a session token ever appears. Opaque 32 bytes, not a JWT.
No token type, no scope, no refresh. This is a DB session handle, not an OAuth response.
The verify body carries no applicantId. The client learns who it is by calling me-routes, not by trusting a login payload.
Cross-agency, proxied from application-service by-applicant. Status and nothing actionable — SLOT_ASSIGNED with no venue and no time anywhere in the platform.
PINS THE GAP. There is no endpoint that returns the citizen's venue or datetime, so a client that expects them here is expecting fiction. GET /v1/applicants/me/slot is proposed, not built.
WITHDRAWN with fromStatus.
Idempotent 200. A client treating only WITHDRAWN as success shows a failure for a repeat click that did what was asked.
NOT_APPLICABLE is a 409, not a member of the 200 union. Modelling it here would let a client render a refusal as a success.
THE CITIZEN'S 401. Distinct code from the JWT kinds' UNAUTHENTICATED, same status, same service.

value.detail: A valid session token is required.

cases.why: Proves the two 401 codes are not interchangeable. A single 401 handler for both credential kinds is wrong.
The officer/system 401 on the same service.
202 both ways — filing is idempotent and the response cannot tell you which happened.
404 NONE means 'you have never filed one'. The normal state for almost every citizen, not an error.
Note the shape: no status-discriminator wrapper. decisionNote is the DPO's ground, deliberately exposed to the citizen.

value.decisionNote: Active application at RDF; retention duty applies.

cases.why: NOT agency-scoped, unlike every application-service officer read. Opaque applicantId only.
The DPO decides without learning who the person is. A name in this queue defeats the design.
A lawful refusal, not an error: a retention duty outranked the erasure right, and the response names who is responsible.
The other ground, with a different field set.
ALREADY_ERASED is a 200, not a 404: the demanded end-state holds.
The DPO decline outcome. Bare status only — the note the officer was forced to write is NOT echoed here; the citizen reads it from GET me/erasure-request instead.
note is MANDATORY. A refusal without a stated ground is a 400 — the UI cannot make that field optional.
Both fields, note within 200.
THREE fields, not one. nationalId and channel travel again alongside the code.
A form that posts only the code fails 400 every time.
